payload.name: Preserve ordinal and temporal cues for creative works
payload.description: When extracting memories about a user's creative work (e.g., screenplay, book, art) and the conversation includes an ordinal like 'third' or a date/time reference, include both the ordinal and the inferred event date in the memory.
content: During extraction from messages about creative projects, if the speaker references an ordinal (first, second, third, etc.) or a start/completion time, record that ordinal as part of the artifact's identity and set the event's world_start to the message date when it indicates the start.
When adding or updating a creative-work memory, include the ordinal (e.g., 'third screenplay') in the content; do not summarize it away into a generic activity statement.

If the user confirms an ordinal in a reply (e.g., 'Yep! ...'), treat the confirmation as explicit evidence and encode it in the same event or profile memory, along with the date context from the session.

solves: The construction pipeline sometimes summarizes creative-work discussions into generic profile/event memories, dropping ordinal identifiers (e.g., 'third', 'second') and concrete temporal references that are explicitly stated or contextually grounded in the conversation. This rule applies whenever a user mentions completing or working on a creative artifact with an ordinal or time cue; the memory should capture the ordinal and, if the surrounding session provides a date, that date as the work's start or completion time. It is not meant for cases where the ordinal or time is absent or ambiguous.
